hints: Group nodes by depth before changing their display direction.
Use a breadth-first queue and snapshot its length for each level.
Read that many nodes, enqueue left then right children, and reverse the row only when its zero-based depth is odd.
Keep the queue order consistent; alternating output direction does not require changing how the next level is discovered.
editorial: Run standard breadth-first traversal, collecting one row at a time. Reverse only rows at odd depths. Queueing children left-to-right independently of display direction prevents one reversed row from corrupting later levels. Every node is processed and reversed at most once. The oracle groups binary position paths by their lengths, sorts positions within each depth, then applies the required parity.
